_comment: Intentional Supabase linter findings. Multiple entries per rule are supported so we can group functions by architectural role with an explicit justification for each bucket. Add a NEW entry (not a new function to an existing bucket) whenever you accept a finding for a new architectural reason. See docs/supabase-lint-allowlist.md for the taxonomy.

allow.name: anon_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: Worker portal RPCs. Field workers scan a share link (no Supabase account) and authenticate per call with share_token + bcrypt PIN; anon EXECUTE IS the auth surface. Each function re-validates token + PIN, scopes to prep_tasks.owner_id, and rate-limits via prep_pin_failures/prep_pin_alerts. Covered by supabase/tests/security_definer_authz.sql (worker-portal group).

allow.name: anon_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: Trigger bodies, not RPCs. Postgres executes triggers with the invoker's session role regardless of EXECUTE grants — the grant on the function is architecturally irrelevant. SECURITY DEFINER is required to read the plan/subscription tables that RLS hides from the writing user. Not directly callable in any meaningful sense; PostgREST invocation returns early because the required TG_OP context is null.

allow.name: anon_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: pg_cron / pgmq worker entry points. Scheduled by the database, not the client; anon EXECUTE exists so pg_cron's `postgres`-role scheduler can enumerate them without extra grants. Functions themselves only read pgmq queues and dispatch — no user-scoped writes and no PII exposure.

allow.name: anon_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: Invoked during the signup handshake before Supabase has issued the authenticated JWT (auth trigger context runs as anon). Each function either derives a value from auth.uid() with an explicit `IF auth.uid() IS NULL THEN RETURN` guard, or looks up a public/plan flag with no PII.

allow.name: anon_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: User RPCs that grant EXECUTE to PUBLIC (so anon inherits) but internally do `IF auth.uid() IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'unauthenticated'` and then scope every read/write to auth.uid() via is_conversation_member / has_role / owner_id checks. Kept on PUBLIC grant historically because these predate the split anon/authenticated grant convention; tightening to `TO authenticated` is tracked as a cleanup but does not change security posture. Covered by supabase/tests/security_definer_authz.sql.

allow.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: First-party user RPCs. SECURITY DEFINER is required because they write to tables (conversations, conversation_members, prep_tasks, friend_requests, subscriptions) whose RLS scopes reads/writes to auth.uid() but need cross-user visibility (e.g. start_dm inserts a row visible to the other party). Each function derives the caller from auth.uid() at the top and rejects null; ownership/membership is validated via is_conversation_member/is_conversation_owner/has_role. Covered by supabase/tests/security_definer_authz.sql.

allow.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: Authorisation predicates used inside RLS policies and other SECURITY DEFINER bodies. They MUST be SECURITY DEFINER to break the RLS recursion loop (see docs/security-definer-inventory.md § predicates). Zero side effects, read-only, return boolean; direct EXECUTE by an authenticated user is equivalent to `SELECT has_role(auth.uid(), 'admin')` which they can already learn from any UI check.

allow.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
allow.reason: Admin-only RPCs. First statement is `IF NOT has_role(auth.uid(), 'admin') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'forbidden'`. SECURITY DEFINER is required to bypass RLS on auth.users / subscriptions / security_findings tables that the admin's own JWT cannot see. Every function in this bucket is exercised by supabase/tests/security_definer_authz.sql (admin-gated group) which asserts a non-admin caller receives `forbidden`.
